case_title: Mahesh Kumar v. State of Haryana
high_court_outcome: Acquitted for mother-in-law, reduced sentence for appellant
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the deceased, was alleged to have subjected her to cruelty and harassment due to dowry demands. The deceased's father and brother provided statements to the police, claiming that the accused and his family demanded dowry and that the deceased was harassed. The deceased sent several letters to her father and brother-in-law, expressing her grievances about the treatment by her in-laws. The deceased died in a hospital, and the police lodged an FIR against the accused and his family. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 304-B IPC, but the High Court acquitted the mother-in-law and reduced the sentence of the accused. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction, finding that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of the offence, including the demand for dowry and the proximity of the harassment to the deceased's death.
